violations.why: timerCount++ in Timer_A is non-atomic; Timer_B can preempt and write, and the increment overwrites it.
Higher-priority Force ISR can write between the read and write of the increment, so the update is lost.
Force ISR writes 0 between the read and write of the increment, so the update is lost.
Timer_B can overwrite timerCount between the increment and the ==1 check.
Force ISR can overwrite timerCount between the increment and the check.
Force ISR sets 0 between the increment and the check, so the check sees a different value.
The value read in the increment can change before the check at line 96 reads it again.
Force ISR can change the value between the two reads.
Force ISR can change the value between the two reads.
Timer_A can modify timerCount between Timer_B's write of 1 and its check.
Force ISR can overwrite timerCount between the write and the check.
Force ISR sets 0 between the write of 1 and the check, so the branch is skipped.
